rows.selection_reason: No experiments have been completed, so there is no evidence to exploit; the priority is to establish a reliable performance baseline at minimal cost. config_001 (RNA-only, single-profile, PCA n2000) is the simplest configuration in the space: it uses a standard linear dimensionality reduction, a single profile, and no learned encoder, making it fast to train and interpret. Running this first gives us a reference accuracy/F1 against which every subsequent design choice (multiprofile aggregation, learned RNA encoders like scVI or scGPT, image modality, and fusion strategy) can be measured for marginal benefit. Because the budget is limited, starting from the cheapest baseline maximizes the number of informative comparisons we can still afford, and it lets us later isolate the effect of each added component (e.g., comparing config_001 vs config_002 to isolate multiprofile+avgpool, or config_001 vs config_016 to isolate adding an image modality with concat fusion) without confounding multiple changes.

Evidence: We have only one completed experiment (config_001: rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000 → acc 0.485, F1 0.464), giving us a weak RNA-only baseline and essentially no information about whether the image modality is informative. Uncertainty: The most critical open question is whether image features carry complementary or superior signal relative to RNA. Question tested: config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) isolates the modality effect by matching config_001 on profile_setting (singleprofile) while switching to the simplest image encoder (resnet50). This is a clean single-variable comparison (RNA vs. image modality). Why this is the best next step: Under a tight budget, knowing whether image is a viable modality determines the entire downstream search strategy—if image is strong, we prioritize image/multimodal configs; if weak, we focus on RNA encoder and profile improvements. Testing a multimodal config now would confound modality, fusion, and aggregation effects, making the result harder to interpret. This experiment maximally reduces uncertainty about the highest-leverage design decision.

Evidence: RNA (pca_n2000, singleprofile) achieves 48.5% acc while image (resnet50, singleprofile) is weak at 20.8%, establishing RNA as the dominant modality. Uncertainty: We have no evidence on whether the profile/aggregation axis (single vs. multiprofile with pooling) improves performance. This experiment (config_002: rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool) directly compares to config_001 by changing only the profile setting and adding avgpool aggregation, isolating the effect of multi-profile representation with a simple, interpretable aggregator. It is the best next step because (1) it keeps the encoder fixed (pca_n2000) for a clean single-axis comparison, (2) the multiprofile+aggregation decision is a structural prerequisite that gates all downstream multimodal multiprofile experiments (configs 018–021, 030–033, etc.), so resolving it early maximizes information value for the remaining budget, and (3) avgpool is the simplest aggregation, giving a conservative baseline before testing transformer aggregation.

Evidence: config_002 (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool) achieved 0.591 acc / 0.573 F1, the best result so far, substantially outperforming the singleprofile baseline (config_001, 0.485 acc). However, the singleprofile→multiprofile jump also introduced an aggregation step, so we cannot yet tell whether the gain comes from the multiprofile representation itself or from the aggregation mechanism. Question: config_003 (multiprofile, pca_n2000, transformer) directly compares transformer aggregation against avgpool while holding all other factors constant, isolating the effect of the aggregation method. Why this is the best next experiment: it is a clean one-variable comparison against our current best, requires no new encoders or modalities, and tells us whether a more expressive aggregation (transformer) is worth the added complexity before we invest budget in learned encoders (scvi, scgpt) or multimodal fusion. If transformer significantly beats avgpool, it signals that richer aggregation is a key design lever; if not, we can focus budget on encoder choice and multimodal combinations with confidence that simple averaging suffices.

Evidence: RNA-only multiprofile+avgpool (config_002, acc=0.591) is the clear best so far, while image-only ResNet50 (config_010, acc=0.208) is very weak. The critical open question is whether the image modality provides complementary information when fused with the strong RNA signal, or whether it merely adds noise. config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, concat) is the minimal extension of config_002: it holds RNA encoder, profile setting, and aggregation identical and introduces only the image branch and concat fusion. This isolates the effect of adding the image modality. If it fails to beat 0.591, we learn that ResNet50 image features are not complementary and can redirect budget toward better RNA encoders or a stronger image encoder (ViT-L). If it does help, it confirms the multimodal direction and justifies further fusion-architecture exploration. Under a tight budget, resolving whether multimodal is worthwhile at all is the highest-value single experiment.

Evidence: RNA (PCA n2000) dominates over image (ResNet50) by a wide margin (0.591 vs 0.208), and the multimodal gain over RNA-only is modest (~0.028). The best RNA-only config (config_002: multi-profile, avgpool) achieves 0.591, but we have no evidence yet about whether a learned RNA encoder (scvi_n200) can capture nonlinear structure that PCA misses. Question: Does scvi_n200 improve over PCA n2000 in the same RNA-only, multi-profile, avgpool setting? This is a clean single-variable comparison against config_002, isolating the RNA encoder effect without confounding from image or fusion choices. Why this is the best next experiment: RNA is the dominant signal source, so understanding whether a learned encoder can push RNA-only performance above 0.591 is the highest-leverage question. If scvi helps here, it will likely compound in the multimodal setting; if it does not, we can rule out RNA encoder complexity as a bottleneck and focus budget on image or fusion improvements. This avoids the risk of changing the RNA encoder in the already-complex multimodal setting where a small effect could be masked by other factors.

Evidence: The best result so far is config_005 (RNA-only, multi-profile, scvi_n200, avgpool) at 0.650 acc / 0.628 F1, showing that scvi_n200 with avgpool aggregation is the strongest RNA configuration. Separately, config_018 (multimodal, multi-profile, PCA, ResNet50, avgpool, concat) at 0.619 shows a modest boost over its RNA-only counterpart config_002 (0.591), suggesting image adds ~3 pts with a weaker RNA encoder. Uncertainty: We do not know whether adding ResNet50 image still helps when the RNA side is already strong (scvi_n200), or whether the weak image signal (image-only acc only 0.208) becomes irrelevant or even detrimental. Question tested: Does the multimodal fusion of scvi_n200 (best RNA) + ResNet50 (best tested image) with avgpool and concat outperform the RNA-only scvi_n200 baseline? This is a single-variable extension of config_005 (adding the image modality), isolating the marginal contribution of image given an optimal RNA pipeline. Why best use of budget: The answer directly determines whether to invest remaining experiments in multimodal variants (configs 031-051) or to focus on RNA-only encoder/aggregation refinements. It is the highest-information experiment because it resolves the central design question—does multimodality add value on top of the best unimodal model—before committing to a large family of multimodal configurations.

Evidence: scvi_n200 is the strongest RNA encoder (config_005: 0.650 acc vs config_002: 0.591 for pca_n2000), avgpool beats transformer for aggregation, and multiprofile beats singleprofile. Surprisingly, adding resnet50 image with concat fusion to the scvi_n200 multimodal model (config_030: 0.632) slightly underperforms the RNA-only version (config_005: 0.650), whereas with pca_n2000 the multimodal concat helped (config_018: 0.619 > config_002: 0.591). This suggests the concat fusion may be the bottleneck when the RNA signal is already strong. Question: Does weighted fusion resolve the multimodal underperformance with scvi_n200? config_031 changes only the fusion strategy (concat→weighted) relative to config_030, giving a clean A/B test of fusion. Why this is best: it isolates a single design variable, directly addresses the most surprising finding (multimodal < unimodal with the best encoder), and determines whether the image modality is salvageable with better fusion or fundamentally unhelpful—critical information before investing further experiments in multimodal variants.

Evidence: RNA is clearly the dominant modality (scvi_n200 rna_only: 0.650 vs image_only resnet50: 0.208), and within RNA, scvi_n200 with avgpool aggregation is the best tested encoder (0.650 vs pca_n2000's 0.591). However, scgpt has been completely untested, leaving a major uncertainty about whether a different RNA representation could outperform scvi_n200. Question: config_008 (rna_only, multiprofile, scgpt, avgpool) is a clean single-variable comparison against config_005 (same setup but scvi_n200), isolating the effect of the RNA encoder while holding profile setting and aggregation constant. Why this is the best next experiment: RNA is the primary signal source, so the encoder choice is the highest-leverage design decision. Resolving whether scgpt is competitive with or superior to scvi_n200 before committing further experiments to multimodal scgpt variants (configs 042-051) avoids wasting budget on a potentially inferior encoder. If scgpt matches or beats scvi_n200, it opens a new high-value direction; if not, we can confidently focus remaining experiments on optimizing the scvi_n200 pipeline (e.g., testing imagenet_vit_l as image encoder in the multimodal setting).

Evidence: The best result so far is config_031 (scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool, weighted, resnet50) at 0.678 acc. A critical unknown remains: we have only tested resnet50 as the image encoder, and image-only resnet50 was very weak (0.208), suggesting the image features may be a bottleneck. The ViT-L encoder is completely untested. Question: config_037 changes only the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l relative to config_031, providing a clean single-variable test of whether a stronger image representation improves the best-known multimodal configuration. Why best next: This is the highest-value uncertainty to resolve. If ViT-L substantially improves performance, it opens a new promising direction; if it does not, it tells us the image modality is inherently limited and we should focus optimization on the RNA side. Either outcome significantly reduces uncertainty about the most important remaining design axis (image encoder quality) while staying in the most promising region of the search space.
